record.why: A refusal that cannot say why is not a refusal. Written 2026-09-03 (lane T fix pass) out of what this record already holds. THE PART IN THIS FOLDER IS PRICED AND IN STOCK: DigiKey FUSB302BMPXCT-ND at USD 1.1000 (1+) down to 0.54316 at 6 000 with 7 075 on hand, LCSC C132291 at USD 0.9413 (1+) down to 0.5068 at 1 000 with 16 140 on hand, both `confidence: verified`, both retrieved 2026-09-02. The refusal is not about those two lines. It is that THIS MPN IS NOT WHAT THE MACHINE FITS: spec/sourcing.json line R1 is 'USB-C CC/PD controller fitted on the Radxa ZERO 3W (reference line — NOT separately purchased)', this record's own matched_on says 'This is the SECOND-SOURCE part, not the fitted one', and component.json's title says the ZERO 3W fits an ET7301B — FUSB302 is the name the device tree uses, not the silicon on the board. The fitted part has NO PRICE AT ANY QUANTITY: this record's first uncertainty is exactly that, its manufacturer datasheet is public (https://www.etekmicro.com/wp-content/uploads/datasheets/ET7301BY_datasheet.pdf) and no distributor carrying it was found. So the folder can quote the alternate and cannot quote the line, and a sourcing record that prices a part the product does not contain has not sourced anything. It also cannot decide the question for itself: whether a re-spin keeps the ET7301B (a Chinese-market part with no Western distribution) or moves to the FUSB302 is a DESIGN decision, not a sourcing one. WHAT SETTLES IT, either of two things: (a) a priced, dated offer for the ET7301B from a distributor that stocks it — then this folder quotes the fitted part and this becomes the alternate; or (b) the design decision to carry the FUSB302BMPX on a Microduck board of our own, recorded in electronics/, after which the two offers already here ARE the quote and this record can say PASS unchanged. Neither is a measurement anyone can take on a distributor page today, which is why it stays CANNOT DETERMINE.
